<strong>Acht von 18 Herkunftsgruppen</st: Eight of 18 origin groups have a district-level breakdown: Turkey, Syria, Kosovo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Iraq, Afghanistan and North Macedonia. They account for around 78 to 83 percent of the state total. The remainder — Pakistan, Morocco, Iran, Lebanon and others — has no district-level figures and is distributed according to migration background.
<strong>Definition der BAMF-Schätzung:</: Definition of the BAMF estimate: People with a migration background from the countries of origin considered, including Alevi adherents. Not all converts and origin groups are covered. The state-level distribution is based on 2019 shares.
<strong>Es gibt daher keine empirisch ab: There is therefore no empirically grounded distribution of the muslim population across districts or municipalities. At the source levels, therefore, selecting a district or municipality does not display a muslim share — instead the figure is marked as missing. The levels “Model by district” and “Model by municipality” distribute the published state total by origin. In the map, profile and export they carry the note “model calculation – not an official religious statistic” and always a range.
<strong>Gemeinden</strong> erhalten kein: Municipalities do not receive their own estimate. The district value is distributed: the Turkish and Bosnian shares follow the settlement pattern measured in the Zensus 2022, the remainder follows the immigration history measured in the Zensus 2022 per municipality. For Syria, Afghanistan, Iraq and Kosovo there is no municipal-level data. The municipal ranges are therefore wider than the district ranges.
<strong>Keine Individualdaten.</strong>: No individual-level data. The project shows exclusively published aggregates or aggregates calculated transparently from them. It contains no residential addresses and no attribution of a religion to individual people.
<strong>T</strong> ist die veröffentlich: T is the published BW range for 2025 (1,133,000–1,197,000). Aₖ,c is the foreign population of citizenship c in district k (Ausländerzentralregister, 31 December 2024). sc is the nationwide muslim share of origin group c (BAMF Forschungsbericht 55, Table 2). rc adds naturalised persons and their descendants born here: persons with a migration background of this origin divided by citizens of the same origin, from the Mikrozensus. MHₖ is the population with a migration background in the district.
<strong>Was das nicht ist:</strong> kein: What this is not: not an official religious statistic, not a survey, not a confidence interval in the statistical sense. The range covers the published state range, the choice of variant and — at municipality level — the choice of distribution key. It does not cover the error in the nationwide origin shares from 2019/2020.
<strong>Zwei Varianten</strong> sind wäh: Two variants are selectable. “Citizenship only” dispenses with rc and distributes the unexplained remainder the same way as the citizenship data itself. The gap between the two variants is part of the uncertainty and is not hidden.

Anteil Ausländerinnen und Ausländer je G: Share of foreign nationals by municipality 2025
Anteil an DE-Modellsumme *: Share of the German model total *
Anteil an allen muslimischen Religionsan: Share of all Muslims in Germany
Anteil an der ausländischen Bevölkerung: Share of the foreign population · naturalised people are missing
Anteil an privater Hauptwohnsitzbevölker: Share of the private main-residence population
Anteil der 18- bis 29-Jährigen an den Ei: Share of 18- to 29-year-olds among the inhabitants of the cell. The map largely traces the university towns — Heidelberg, Tübingen, Freiburg, Konstanz — and alongside them the inner-city districts of the larger cities. It works as a counter-image to the foreign-national layer: where both are high there is usually a university, and that is something other than an immigrant district. Shares only from 30 inhabitants per cell upwards.
Anteil der Ausländerinnen und Ausländer: Share of the foreign nationals in the district
Anteil der Bevölkerung ohne deutsche Sta: Share of the population without German citizenship per government region (NUTS 2), added up from the district figures. Naturalised persons and descendants born here hold a German passport and do not appear in these figures.

Share of the population without German citizenship, reference date 31 December 2025. The same measure as the 2024 layer, one year later and updated by the federal government instead of the state. The difference is small: the median across districts is 17.2 percent in both years, and the largest deviation for any district is 0.4 percentage points. Both layers stand side by side so this can be checked rather than simply asserted.
Share of the population without German citizenship. Calculated in-house from concurrent official register data. No indication of religion, country of birth, or parents' origin.
Anteil der Einwohnerinnen und Einwohner: Share of residents without German citizenship, by municipality. Naturalised persons and their children born in Germany count as Germans and are invisible here — in long-established communities that is the majority. A municipality with a low share of foreign nationals can still have a long-established immigrant population. This is measured, not modelled: the only directly recorded figure the atlas can place alongside the model calculation at municipality level.
Anteil der Erwerbspersonen — erwerbstäti: Share of the labour force — in work, or unemployed and looking — among the foreign-born aged 20 to 64. The difference from the unemployment rate is the whole point: someone who neither works nor looks for work appears in no unemployment rate. Two regions with the same unemployment rate can therefore look very different, and the gap to the native-born is shown in the profile.
Anteil der Erwerbstätigen an der Bevölke: Share of employed persons among the population aged 15 and over with a migration background. Sample survey. No unemployment rate, because the source withholds the number of unemployed persons for almost all districts for confidentiality. These figures do not feed into any model calculation in this atlas.
Anteil der Menschen mit türkischer Staat: Share of people with Turkish citizenship among the inhabitants of the cell. Three things this map does NOT show. First, no religion: Turkish citizenship is not a religious affiliation, and the census records none. Second, not people of Turkish origin: most of them hold a German passport in Baden-Württemberg and are absent here entirely — what the map shows is the smaller, non-naturalised part. Third, no completeness: only 6,581 of the 21,585 inhabited cells carry a value, and an empty cell means either nobody or too few to be allowed to say. Shares are formed only from 30 inhabitants per cell upwards, because secrecy shifts small numbers by exactly the order of magnitude at stake.
Anteil der Menschen ohne deutschen Pass: Share of people without a German passport per grid cell of one kilometre. A municipality like Stuttgart has a single value for 610,000 inhabitants on every other layer of this atlas; only here can you see how different its neighbourhoods are. Empty areas are two things at once and cannot be told apart: uninhabited, or kept secret. The census suppresses small cases and perturbs the rest using the cell-key method — of 21,585 inhabited cells only 13,516 carry a foreign-national share. Reading the gaps as empty land misreads the map.
Anteil der Mitglieder der evangelischen: Share of members of the Protestant church in the population, from the 2022 census. The mirror image of the layer beside it, and almost literally so: together the two maps show the confessional boundary of 1555, still visible in the settlement pattern today. 25.9 per cent statewide; both churches together 55.8 per cent.
Anteil der Mitglieder der römisch-kathol: Share of members of the Roman Catholic church in the population, from the 2022 census. This is the most pronounced religious structure Baden-Württemberg has: Catholic Upper Swabia and the south against Protestant old Württemberg. 29.9 per cent statewide. Counted, not estimated — unlike the Muslim population, for which no survey exists at municipal level. Individual values are protected by the cell-key method and are therefore deliberately slightly perturbed.
Anteil der Mitglieder evangelischer Frei: Share of members of Protestant free churches in the district population, 2011 Census — the second group the 2022 Census lets disappear into the residual category. 1.1 per cent statewide, a good 119,000 people. The layer is here because free churches come up repeatedly in this atlas’s surveys: in the KONID survey, respondents counted among them agree more often than any other group that their own religion takes precedence over the constitution in case of conflict. How large the group being talked about there is, this map says.
Anteil der Mitglieder orthodoxer Kirchen: Share of members of Orthodox churches in the district population, 2011 Census. This is the only count there is for them: the 2022 Census no longer reports the public-law religious societies separately but puts everything except the two large churches into one residual category. In 2011 Baden-Württemberg had the highest Orthodox population share of any state at 2.1 per cent, against 1.3 per cent nationally; the peak is Stuttgart at 5.3 per cent. Three limits belong to every one of these figures. What is counted is registered membership of a public-law corporation, not who considers themselves Orthodox — which church holds that status differs from church to church and from state to state, and the Syriac Orthodox Church, for instance, appears only where it has it. And the reference date is 9 May 2011: the arrivals from Romania, Bulgaria, Syria, Iraq and Ukraine came after it. The map is therefore a lower bound, not a present state. One category is missing here altogether: no Islamic community holds corporation status in Baden-Württemberg, so Muslims appear in the row „Member of no public-law religious society“ — together with everyone of no faith.
Anteil der Personen ohne Pass des Wohnsi: Share of people without a passport of the country they live in. This is the same definition used on the district and municipal layers of this atlas — unlike country of birth, naturalised citizens are not counted here. What is comparable is the definition, not the number: Eurostat counts only people aged 15 to 64 in private households, and because immigrants are over-represented in those age groups the value is higher than the share across all ages. For the Stuttgart region 25.3 instead of 19.8 per cent.
Anteil der ausländischen Bevölkerung des: Share of the district's foreign population holding Turkish citizenship. Not the number of people of Turkish origin: naturalised persons and their descendants born here hold a German passport and are entirely absent. Nationwide median: 7.5 percent.

Share of the district's foreign population originating from the guest-worker recruitment countries — Turkey, Italy, Greece, Spain, Portugal, Morocco, Tunisia, former Yugoslavia. The denominator is the district's foreign population, not its total population.

Share of the district's foreign population that has lived in Germany for at least 25 years. This figure, too, counts only people without a German passport — precisely among the long-established, naturalised persons are missing, so the length of stay of origin groups tends to be underestimated. Nationwide median: 17.4 percent.
Anteil der ausländischen Bevölkerung mit: Share of the foreign population resident for at least 25 years — the counterpart to the district layer of the same name, one level up. Baden-Württemberg ranks first of all states at 27.4 per cent: its foreign population is longer established than anywhere else. In the east the value lies between 4 and 7 per cent. This measure in particular understates length of residence, because those here longest are the most likely to have been naturalised and then leave the register.
Anteil der hier geborenen Menschen mit d: Share of people born here with a German passport among the population with a migration background. These are precisely the people missing from the foreign-national statistics — which is why the model calculation needs a correction for naturalised persons and descendants. No indication of religious affiliation.
Anteil der im Ausland Geborenen an der B: Share of foreign-born people among the population aged 15 to 64 in private households. What is counted is the place of birth, not the passport: naturalised citizens are included here and are not included in the foreign-national share of the other layers. Labour Force Survey sample; correspondingly uncertain for small regions.
Anteil der in Deutschland Geborenen an d: Share of people born in Germany among the state’s foreign population. The usual objection to any passport-based figure is that those born here are missing — here it is quantified, as far as they hold no German passport. North Rhine-Westphalia leads with 15.0 per cent, Baden-Württemberg follows with 13.2; in the eastern states the value is 7 to 9 per cent because immigration there is more recent. Not included are naturalised people and children who become German at birth under section 4(3) of the Nationality Act.
Anteil der unter 25-Jährigen an der Bevö: Share of people under 25 among the population with a migration background. Hatched: the source withholds too many age groups to form a reliable share. Migration background is a far larger group than the modelled muslim population; this is not that group's age structure.

Share of people under 25 in the population, from the Zensus 2022. Unlike the district layer from the Mikrozensus, this is a full census and available for all municipalities. No indication of religious affiliation and not a variable in the model calculation.
Anteil der unter 25-Jährigen an der ausl: Share of people under 25 among the district's foreign population. Statewide this is 24.6 percent — 24.9 percent for the German population, so practically the same. This is partly an artefact of how the count works: children of immigrants who are naturalised or born German count on the German side and are missing on the foreign side. This is explicitly not a comparison of the age structure of origin groups.
Anteil derer, die 2010 oder später einge: Share of those who arrived in 2010 or later among the foreign-born whose year of arrival is known. A high value means recent immigration, a low one a long-established population — the counterpart to the district layer "resident for 25 years", except that there the passport counts and here the place of birth. From the 2021 census: a full count across all ages, not a sample estimate, but a single snapshot with no update. Cases with no year of arrival are left out of the denominator rather than quietly counted among the long-established; their share is shown in each region's profile. In 15 of the 251 regions — in Czechia, France and Slovakia — it is missing for more than a fifth, in Baden-Württemberg for at most a tenth.
Anteil mit tertiärem Abschluss an den im: Share with a tertiary qualification among the foreign-born aged 25 to 64. This layer separates out one of the four things bundled into the employment rate gap. It also shows what an average conceals: in the Stuttgart region 28.7 per cent of the foreign-born hold a university degree and 35.0 per cent have at most lower secondary education — the group is strongly represented at both ends, not in the middle. Both figures and the gap to the native-born are in each region's profile.
Anteile beziehen sich auf die ausländisc: Shares refer to the district's foreign population, not its total population.
Antworten auf Fragen, nicht gezählte Men: Answers to questions, not counted people. A section of its own, because one percentage looks like another and no one can see from a bar whether a register or a questionnaire lies behind it.

Die Region ist die Ebene NUTS 2 der euro: The region is level NUTS 2 of the European territorial classification. Its figures are added up from the district figures, not newly collected.
Die Restkategorie des Zensus: alle, die: The residual category of the census: everyone belonging to neither the Roman Catholic nor the Protestant church. That means people with no denomination, all other religions and all missing answers in a single figure. This layer is therefore NEITHER a share of the non-religious NOR a Muslim share, and must not be read as one. Its value for this atlas is different: because Muslim residents necessarily fall under it, the modelled Muslim share of a municipality cannot exceed this value. The layer thus makes visible what the model has so far only been checked against arithmetically. 44.2 per cent statewide.
Die Seite wird über GitHub Pages ausgeli: The site is delivered via GitHub Pages. In doing so, the host may process the usual connection data such as IP address, time and the file requested. This project has no influence over that.
Die Werte stehen nebeneinander, weil sie: The figures stand side by side because they were published, not because they measure the same thing. Different bodies, different methods, different definitions of who counts as Muslim. A line drawn through these points is supported by none of the sources.
Die abweichenden Tabelle-1-Werte werden: The diverging Table 1 figures are not used here for the calculation.
Die beiden Landesumfragen von 2012 und 2: The two state surveys of 2012 and 2019 cover different populations: in 2012 Germans aged 18 and over, that is eligible voters, were surveyed; in 2019 German-speaking people aged 18 and over. Reading the values as a development also compares two differently defined populations. The state report points this out itself.
Die dargestellten Werte sind keine amtli: The figures shown are not an official statistic. For decisions with legal or financial consequences, the respective original source must be consulted.
Die einheitliche Landesfläche bedeutet n: A uniform state-wide area does not mean that every district has the same muslim share. Corresponding source data for districts and municipalities is not available.
Die einzige Alterspyramide dieses Atlas: The only age pyramid in this atlas is the one beside it: by immigration history, from the microcensus, for Baden-Württemberg, across all ages — and with no religious affiliation at all.
Die historischen BW-Werte stammen aus: <: The historical BW figures come from: Statistisches Monatsheft Baden-Württemberg 4/2020, S. 3–10.
Die verbreitete KMK-Zahl — für 2023/24 9: The widely quoted KMK figure — 9,750 for 2023/24 — does not include upper secondary level. The difference from 10,060 is exactly that level.
Die veröffentlichte Landessumme wird nac: The published state total is distributed by origin: foreign population by citizenship multiplied by the nationwide muslim share of that origin group, corrected for naturalised persons. The model does not invent a total and does not measure religious affiliation. Every area carries a range.
Die vier Regierungsbezirke sind die Eben: The four government regions are level NUTS 2 of the European territorial classification. The figures are added up from the district figures, not newly collected.
Dies ist keine vollständige Validierung: This is not a complete validation of the projection model.
Diese Anwendung hat keine Konten, keine: This application has no accounts, no cookies, no analytics or tracking services and no advertising. Selection, calculations and exports run entirely in the browser; no input is sent to a server, geocoding service or AI service. No fonts, map tiles or program libraries are loaded from third-party servers.
Diese Zahlen gehen in keine Modellrechnu: These figures feed no calculation in this atlas and are not combined with any population figure.
Diese beiden Länder wurden bei der Stich: These two states were combined when the sample was drawn and can only be reported jointly. The value applies to both together, not to either one of them.
Dieselbe Aufzählung der 39 ADÜTDF-Verein: The same list of the 39 ADÜTDF associations five days earlier, plus 55 local IGMG associations named individually. This Drucksache, too, does not give addresses; they are documented individually for each entry. As of 2011
Dieselbe Bevölkerung wie die Ebene daneb: The same population as the layer beside it, more narrowly defined: only those born outside the EU-27. The difference between the two layers is migration from other EU states, which in law is something entirely different from migration from outside.
Dieselbe Frage eine Ebene höher, und dor: The same question one level up, and there it becomes clearer still: the two bodies cross over. Pew estimates fewer Muslims for 2010 than the BAMF does for 2008, but more for 2016 than the BAMF does for 2015. Reading either series on its own means mistaking its course for the course of the matter itself.
Dieselbe Methode wie das Modell daneben,: The same method as the model alongside it, but with all 18 origin groups from the BAMF report instead of the eight the state report names per district. The origin data thus accounts for 96 instead of 83 percent of the published state total; the remainder, which must be distributed using a substitute key, shrinks from a sixth to under four percent. Both models stand side by side because the difference between them makes visible the uncertainty inherent in both: it averages 0.46 percentage points and reaches 1.7 in Heidelberg. Wortlaut der drei Aussagen: „Christen [M: Wording of the three statements: „Christians [Muslims] should return to the roots of Christianity [Islam].“ · „There is only one interpretation of the Bible [the Koran] and all Christians [Muslims] must abide by it.“ · „The rules of the Bible [the Koran] matter more to me than the laws of Germany.“ This sample is not a sample of Muslims in Germany. Only people of Turkish and Moroccan origin whose parents or grandparents immigrated before 1975 were surveyed; half of the Turkish-origin respondents come from particular rural regions of central and eastern Anatolia. Koopmans himself writes that the data may therefore not be nationally representative. The native-born comparison group was not subject to these restrictions — so the comparison is not symmetrical. In Germany 489 people of Turkish and 479 of Moroccan origin were surveyed, around 9,000 in all across six countries; 96 per cent of respondents of Turkish or Moroccan origin described themselves as Muslim, 70 per cent of the native-born as Christian. Bases per bar are not published. Taken statement by statement, agreement among the Muslims surveyed is almost 60 per cent (return to the roots), 75 per cent (only one interpretation) and 65 per cent (religious rules before secular law); for native-born Christians the text gives a range of 13 to 21 per cent across the individual statements. Because the Christian figures per statement are not published as single numbers, the chart shows only the measure stated exactly for every group: agreement with all three statements at once.

In Baden-Württemberg 11,827 in the 2025/26 school year, denominational and run by the Stiftung Sunnitischer Schulrat — the third highest figure, after North Rhine-Westphalia and Bavaria. The map does, however, largely reflect the size of the states: the more telling figure would be the share of Muslim pupils reached, and only seven states record it at all — where it exists, it is in the profile. Not an official consolidated statistic: the ministries answer individually. Bremen and Hamburg teach across denominations and do not report Islamic participation separately; the five eastern states offer none. Berlin and Schleswig-Holstein still report 2024/25, and Bavaria's figure is rounded. The state figures sum exactly to the published national total of 84,356 — every retrieval is checked against it.
